A1.justification: Both PDFs describe LTE, with readable text, equations, tables, figures and complete appendices. Retained material can be matched reliably across relocation and renumbering.

before.justification: v2 reports original Qwen3-4B/8B training experiments, six-benchmark evaluations, training dynamics and hint ablations.

after.justification: v4 retains those experiments and adds SciQ results, training-cost comparisons and algorithm-component ablations.

M1.justification: The hint templates, random replacement, Algorithm 1 and mixed-policy objectives remain unchanged. The expanded explanation of hinted-policy sampling and relocated implementation approximations do not change the proposed procedure; the new variants are ablations.

E1.justification: v4 extends evaluation beyond mathematical reasoning to science-examination questions on SciQ validation and test sets (Section 5.6, Table 6). The original mathematical training dataset and six evaluation benchmarks remain.

E2.justification: The main baseline roster remains Base, GRPO, GRPOExtra, EvoCoT, ReLIFT, DAPO and LUFFY. New appendix comparisons introduce LTE variants without off-policy treatment, importance sampling or policy shaping as additional comparison controls (Tables 9–10), without adding an external baseline.

E3.justification: v4 adds a cost-matching evaluation using intermediate LTE checkpoints at 300 or 400 steps against 500-step baselines, plus SciQ evaluation with an 8,192-token response limit. Existing mathematical protocols remain unchanged. Conflicting runtimes in Tables 3–4 prevent verification of the claimed budget equivalence.

E4.justification: New analyses examine training cost and performance under approximately matched budgets, and ablate off-policy optimization, importance sampling and policy shaping (Section 5.4; Appendices D–E). The original hint ablation is retained as Table 5, with 'Overlong' renamed 'Concise' and identical results.

E5.justification: The existing four- and sixteen-response evaluation practices remain unchanged. Neither version reports training-seed repetitions, empirical confidence intervals, error bars or significance tests; the added experiments continue point-estimate reporting.

E6.justification: Tables 1–2, the original hint-ablation results and plotted training dynamics are unchanged. v4 adds runtime and intermediate-checkpoint results, SciQ scores and component-ablation outcomes. For example, SciQ test Pass@1/Pass@4 is 57.75/59.83 for LTE versus 55.43/57.35 for GRPO; removing policy shaping yields 40.26/57.23 versus LTE's retained 39.62/55.61 mathematical averages.

T1.justification: Appendix A's definitions, assumptions and derivation are unchanged, as are the existing objective equations. The new hinted-policy notation restates the sampling distribution already represented in Equation 6; the random-replacement discussion adds an informal rationale rather than a proof.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same central contributions: self-generated error hints mitigate exploration stagnation without external expert reasoning traces. The headline 5.02 Pass@1 and 9.96 Pass@k improvements remain; the new experiments support these retained claims.

C2.justification: v4 adds interpretations concerning acceptable computational overhead, learning effectiveness within matched budgets, component necessity and the lack of benefit from policy shaping. Appendix B argues that random replacement is necessary for consistent groups and distributed training. Applicability expands from mathematics to short-answer mathematics/science, while longer outputs and multi-turn interactions remain limitations; Section 5.3 also corrects entropy collapse to arise from lacking explicit entropy control.

D1.justification: v4 replaces the advertised anonymous code location with the GitHub project JamyDon/LTE and discloses baseline runtimes and component-ablation procedures. Hardware and common hyperparameters are retained; gamma, the old-policy approximation and Math-Verify information are relocated rather than newly introduced.

R1.justification: v4 adds Schulman et al. (2015) for importance sampling and Welbl et al. (2017) for SciQ, while removing Cheng et al. (2025) and its entropy-advantage discussion. The four related-work categories and LTE's principal positioning remain.

P1.justification: There are localized copyedits, an introductory roadmap, expanded sampling explanations, labeled limitations and revised author/acknowledgment text. Implementation passages move to Appendix C, but the main narrative and section ordering remain largely intact.

P2.justification: v4 substantially expands the tabular presentation with dedicated runtime, cost-matched performance, SciQ and component-ablation tables (Tables 3, 4, 6, 9 and 10). Existing tables and Figure 4 are relocated, while the original diagrams and plotted curves are retained.

improvement.justification: SciQ evaluation and component ablations provide useful evidence beyond v2's mathematical benchmarks and hint ablations, improving coverage and understanding of LTE. The gain is limited by inconsistencies in the new efficiency analysis: Table 3 assigns GRPO 5/7 days to 4B/8B, whereas Table 4 reverses those runtimes. Consequently, the claimed budget alignment is not reliably established.
